security_audit.summary: Forty static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline code, fixed documentation links, and GitHub metadata. One command is confirmed because SKILL.md instructs the agent to run a Resend connector that can perform a live suppression mutation.

remediation.issue: The Resend workflow can execute a live external mutation through the connector command.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval immediately before --live, validate the target, display the dry-run result, and confirm the affected account.

content.value_statement: Email teams often struggle to turn disconnected exports into reliable audiences. This skill creates measurable segments, lifecycle stages, RFM tiers, and suppression rules.
actual_capabilities: Profiles available columns in CRM, email platform, analytics, and ecommerce exports.
Builds behavioral audiences from opens, clicks, browsing, carts, and purchases.
Creates RFM tiers from user-provided recency, frequency, and monetary fields.
Maps subscribers into reusable new, active, at-risk, lapsed, and win-back stages.
Reconciles unsubscribes, hard bounces, complaints, and consent withdrawals into suppression rules.
Labels segment counts as measured or estimated and explains each calculation.
limitations: Requires user-provided exports or accessible consent records; it does not discover missing data automatically.
Cannot build valid RFM tiers without recency, frequency, and monetary order fields.
Does not send campaigns, write creative, design flows, or audit deliverability.
Live platform synchronization depends on an available connector and separate user authorization.

use_cases.title: Prepare retention audiences
use_cases.description: Create engaged, at-risk, lapsed, and win-back cohorts from recent activity and purchase data.

use_cases.title: Protect campaign compliance
use_cases.description: Reconcile consent, unsubscribe, bounce, and complaint records before building a mailable audience.

use_cases.title: Standardize customer tiers
use_cases.description: Convert order history into reusable RFM and lifecycle definitions for campaign planning.

prompt_templates.title: Create basic engagement segments
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this email export and create engaged, inactive, and suppression segments. Label every count as measured or estimated.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has one subscriber export.

prompt_templates.title: Build retention lifecycle stages
prompt_templates.prompt: Map these CRM and campaign exports into new, active, at-risk, lapsed, and win-back stages. State each rule and missing field.
prompt_templates.scenario: A retention team needs reusable lifecycle audiences.

prompt_templates.title: Develop RFM audience tiers
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these order fields to create RFM tiers. Explain thresholds, counts, overlaps, and suppression exclusions without exposing customer records.
prompt_templates.scenario: An ecommerce team has complete order history.

prompt_templates.title: Design a governed segment framework
prompt_templates.prompt: Combine CRM, engagement, order, and consent exports into behavioral, RFM, lifecycle, and suppression segments. Resolve conflicts and document assumptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced team needs a governed segmentation framework.

output_examples.input: Subscriber export with last click, opt-in status, bounce status, and signup date.
output_examples.output: Engaged 90 days: 12,480 measured members. Suppression: 638 measured members from unsubscribes and hard bounces. Purchase-based tiers need order data.

output_examples.input: CRM and order exports containing purchase dates, order counts, revenue, and consent status.
output_examples.output: Champions: recent, frequent, high-value customers. At-risk: previously active customers with declining recency. All consent withdrawals remain suppressed.

output_examples.input: Campaign export without consent timestamps or complaint flags.
output_examples.output: Engagement segments are available. Consent-sensitive cohorts are marked NEEDS_INPUT, and no mailable status is assumed.

best_practices: Provide column definitions and reporting dates with every export.
Use the consent registry as the source of truth for suppression decisions.
Review estimated counts and obtain approval before saving or synchronizing segments.
anti_patterns: Do not paste instructions from untrusted CSV cells into agent prompts.
Do not assume subscribers are opted in when consent records are missing.
Do not include raw email addresses or phone numbers in summaries.

faq.question: Which files can this skill use?
faq.answer: It can use user-provided CRM, email platform, GA4, ecommerce, and consent exports with relevant columns.

faq.question: Does it send email campaigns?
faq.answer: No. It defines audiences and suppression rules but does not compose, schedule, or send messages.

faq.question: How are segment sizes reported?
faq.answer: Each size is labeled measured when counted from data or estimated when inferred with a stated method.

faq.question: What happens when consent data is missing?
faq.answer: The affected cohort is marked NEEDS_INPUT. The skill does not assume that those subscribers are mailable.

faq.question: Can it create RFM tiers without order data?
faq.answer: No. RFM tiers require recency, frequency, and monetary fields from owned order data.

faq.question: Can it synchronize segments to an email platform?
faq.answer: Optional connectors may support synchronization. Live changes require connector availability, valid authorization, and explicit user approval.
